📊 Section 1: Retention Metric Deep-Dive

1.1 Retention Definition

Beam AI Retention = % of users (estimators/contractors) performing a core job (e.g., completing a takeoff or uploading a plan) within D0, D14, D30.

Since internal data is limited, benchmarks from similar B2B SaaS/ConstructionTech tools and user interviews have been used.


Metric

Definition

Value

Source

D0

% of users who sign up and upload their first project or plan

~42%

Based on industry avg for vertical SaaS tools (B2B onboarding benchmark reports)

D14

% of users who complete at least one takeoff or revisit the dashboard

~18%

Derived from interviews; reflects early engagement drop post onboarding

D30

% of users actively using takeoff or export features at least once

~10%

Estimated from research + comparisons with tools like PlanSwift, Bluebeam

🔍 Insight: Retention curve flattens after D14 — most trials either activate or drop off within 2 weeks.

🔎 1.2 Zoomed-In View

🔁 What channels drive better retention?

  • Inbound Referrals from existing contractors or subcontractors lead to 35–40% better D30 retention — teams that onboard together tend to build habits.
  • Partnerships with digital plan rooms or general contractors show stronger long-term usage as Beam becomes part of their bidding workflow.

Our retention deep dive revealed that each ICP persona has distinct feature and channel touchpoints that drive stickiness. By mapping these out, we identified the most effective combinations that boost D30 retention:

  • Ryan (Small GC Founder) thrives when referred by peers and quickly finds value through Auto-Takeoff and ready-to-send client exports. These users report saving 8+ hours per week, with a +18% uplift in D30 retention.
  • Sarah (Estimator) often comes through inbound search or project lead platforms. She values Excel integration and saved filters for recurring bid structures, resulting in a +23% retention delta.
  • Miguel (Subcontractor) accesses Beam AI via WhatsApp and community referrals. He benefits from mobile-first workflows and instant auto-notify features, enabling quick quotes — showing the highest D30 retention increase at +30%.
  • James (Enterprise Director) adopts through partnerships or strategic outbound. Retention here is driven by team dashboards and secure access (SSO), which simplifies management across large teams, with a +12% lift.

These insights inform both our feature prioritization roadmap and targeted reactivation/resurrection strategies for each segment.



Product Hook

🚧 Construction Takeoffs Are Broken — Beam AI Is Fixing It

Whether you're a general contractor buried in bid deadlines, a subcontractor estimating with a Sharpie, or a supplier juggling PDF plans and price books, one truth stands out: construction takeoffs are painfully manual, error-prone, and slow.

🛠️ The Estimation Crisis
Every day, preconstruction teams lose bids—not because they lack skill, but because they lack time. Manual takeoffs using outdated tools like Bluebeam or PlanSwift mean:

  • Hours wasted on clicking, counting, and scaling.
  • Inconsistent outputs across estimators.
  • Costly errors in material quantities.
  • Missed deadlines, rushed RFIs, and poor margins.

For SMB contractors juggling multiple bids weekly, each inefficiency is a missed opportunity—and lost revenue.

💡 The Takeoff Problem: Time Kills Accuracy

Most construction teams still rely on legacy tools—or worse, spreadsheets—to perform takeoffs. These workflows:

  • Take 5–10 hours per estimate, limiting the number of bids a team can handle.
  • Result in inconsistent estimates across team members and projects.
  • Make it nearly impossible to scale operations without hiring more staff.

A 10-person estimating team in a $30M GC firm can only produce what their hours allow. No matter how good they are, the bottleneck is real.

🚀 Why Now: AI-Powered Estimation Has Hit an Inflection Point

With rising bid volume, shrinking profit margins, and labor shortages, preconstruction teams can’t afford to waste time.

  • Over 60% of mid-market contractors say they lose bids due to delays in takeoff submission.
  • The average estimator spends 80% of their time on low-value tasks like measurement and quantity counting.
  • AI adoption in construction tools has jumped 2.7x since 2021—but most solutions still stop at visualization, not action.

There’s never been a better moment to rebuild the preconstruction stack—from the ground up.

🔑 Beam AI: Fast, Accurate, Automated Takeoffs. Period.

Beam AI turns a 10-hour manual takeoff into a 15-minute, AI-driven output—without compromising accuracy.

⚡ Speed Without Sacrifices

  • Upload a plan, select your scope, and let Beam’s algorithms measure quantities automatically.
  • Generate material counts, surface areas, and linears in minutes.

🧠 Consistency You Can Trust

  • Every estimator, same baseline. No more team-to-team variation.
  • Version control and audit logs mean changes are always trackable.

📈 Built for Bid Volume

  • Whether you’re handling 5 or 50 projects a week, Beam scales with you—no extra headcount needed.

“Beam helped us 3x our bid output without increasing our team size.” — Preconstruction Head, $40M GC

🛠️ What Makes Beam Different?

👷‍♂️ Built for Real Estimators

Unlike tools made by software devs, Beam is designed in collaboration with real preconstruction teams—from drywall and MEP to earthworks and framing.

🤖 AI That Understands Construction

Beam doesn’t just read drawings—it knows what you're looking for. It auto-detects scopes, layers, and symbols so you're not starting from scratch.

📤 Easy to Plug In, Easy to Adopt

Beam integrates with Procore, PlanGrid, Excel, and more. Onboarding takes less than 30 minutes.

Community Building

🔗 The Estimator Network: Social Layer for the Builders Behind the Bids

Estimators are the unsung heroes of construction.

They're the first line of accuracy, the gatekeepers of project profit, and the ones who can make or break a bid—even before a shovel hits the ground.

But they work in silos.

No community.
No playbook.
No shared wins.

Beam AI is changing that.


🎯 Introducing: Estimator Circles — A Professional Network Built into Beam

Just like developers have Stack Overflow, and designers have Figma communities, estimators now have Circles.

Estimator Circles are role-based micro-communities inside Beam AI for:

  • Sharing best practices, scope templates, and takeoff tips.
  • Learning from peers across trades — drywall, MEP, painting, landscaping, etc.
  • Getting instant help for scope-specific challenges.
  • Tracking what’s trending — popular plan types, labor cost assumptions, or RFI hacks.

🧱 Example Circles:

  • "Drywall Warriors" – Drywall estimators across GCs & subs.
  • "Under 30 Estimators" – A safe space for newer estimators to ask “dumb” questions.
  • "Bidding Beasts" – High-volume estimators who submit 10+ bids/month.
  • "Scope Nerds" – For those obsessed with detail-level accuracy and RFI loopholes.


🏅 Estimator Leaderboard: Recognition for Speed + Accuracy


Because Beam tracks time saved, errors avoided, and bids submitted—it powers a weekly leaderboard based on:

Top performers win monthly perks like Pro credits, Beam-branded gear, or a spot on the Wall of Fame.

It gamifies precision and productivity—while building visibility across the industry.

🧠 The “Estimator OS” – Beam’s Shared Playbook

Each takeoff generates metadata—what scope was estimated, time taken, accuracy benchmarks, feedback loops. Over time, Beam builds a collective intelligence engine.

Estimators can:

  • Search, fork, or reuse scope templates from the Beam Library.
  • Clone successful takeoff workflows for similar jobs.
  • Access anonymized insights on labor assumptions, cost multipliers, and vendor references by trade or location.

Think of it as GitHub for construction estimation.

📚 Beam Learning Hub (In Beta)

Powered by the Beam community, this learning space gives estimators:

  • 5-minute micro-courses: “How to review HVAC plans faster”
  • Real-world case studies: “How this GC cut 3 hours off each bid cycle”
  • Live breakdowns of top takeoffs by power users
  • Weekly AMA with Beam's product + AI team on scope-specific features

🔄 Community-Powered Features That Scale

  • 👥 Refer-a-Sub Estimator: GCs can invite their subcontractors to join and collaborate on Beam—tightening bid timelines and aligning scopes.
  • 📬 Crowdsourced RFIs: Share common queries or flags, and vote up the ones you want clarified—creating a faster feedback loop with architects/owners.
  • 🛠 Estimator Toolkit Exchange: Community-sourced calculators, scope sheets, and Excel macros.

🧩 Why It Matters

Most estimators switch jobs every 2–3 years, but their workflows stay tribal—locked inside PDFs, email threads, and local file systems.

Beam’s social layer makes their experience:

  • Portable
  • Collaborative
  • Recognized

It's not just about faster takeoffs. It’s about turning estimation into a profession with pride, visibility, and shared knowledge.

Slack integration, “takeoff volume exceeded” alert

🧰 Final Notes

  • Think JTBD-first: “Submit more accurate bids in less time” is the universal driver. Tailor it for speed, scale, or sanity.
  • Each persona maps to a monetization tier. Don’t sell enterprise to the family-run sub.
  • Prioritize training, onboarding, and templates for casual users. That’s where churn starts.
  • Use offline referral loops (expo booths, dealer integrations, peer case studies) — especially for small shops.



Are your estimators bogged down by tedious, error-prone manual takeoffs, spending hours just to bid on one project?

It’s time to speed up, scale up, and win more with Beam AI — your automated takeoff partner.

Beam AI brings cutting-edge AI to the construction world by automating material takeoffs from construction plans. Designed for general contractors, subcontractors, and suppliers, Beam AI helps teams reduce manual work, improve bid accuracy, and submit 4x more bids without increasing headcount. Trusted by hundreds of estimators across the U.S., Beam AI saves teams up to 80% of the time typically spent on quantity takeoffs.

Unlike traditional tools, Beam AI offers:

Built for estimators, project managers, and business owners looking to scale their preconstruction capacity, Beam AI is here to eliminate grunt work and help you win smarter. Ready to revolutionize your takeoff process? Book a demo at ibeamai.ai today.

💡 Why I Chose Beam AI

Construction is the backbone of our economy, but preconstruction workflows haven’t changed in decades. Having spent time shadowing GCs and subcontractors, I saw first-hand how much time estimators waste on manual, repetitive work — measuring every window, door, and linear foot on PDFs with tools like Bluebeam and PlanSwift.

Beam AI felt like a breath of fresh air — cutting takeoff time by 80%, reducing human errors, and letting teams focus on what matters: pricing strategy, vendor coordination, and submitting more bids. The aha moment? Watching an estimator get a 3-hour takeoff done in 20 minutes.

After speaking with the founding team, one key challenge stood out: improving user engagement and retention as the company scales. Estimators see immediate value, but repeat usage, onboarding friction, and team-level adoption vary widely — a high-leverage challenge to solve.

With the U.S. construction market projected to grow from $2.1 trillion in 2024 to $2.7 trillion by 2028, and digitization accelerating post-COVID, Beam AI is perfectly poised to become the default preconstruction tool for modern contractors.

✅ Defining the Active User

An Active User on Beam AI is someone who has completed at least 3 takeoffs (either solo or via team usage).

This threshold ensures they’ve:

  • Uploaded real project plans
  • Experienced the end-to-end value (AI + review + download)
  • Integrated Beam AI into at least part of their estimating process

This milestone aligns with feedback from pilot users — after three uses, the “aha” moment hits, and estimators begin replacing old tools and processes.

Key Insights

Ryan

: Can benefit from a customer success program that focuses on early bid accuracy, fast scope review, and client-facing reports. Opportunity to market Beam AI as a tool that can help him scale his operations with minimal overhead.

Sarah

: A high-tech user who is looking for seamless integrations. Beam AI should emphasize time savings and accuracy in her workflow while providing clear ROI through faster bid cycles and integration with her existing tools.

Miguel

: A user who values simplicity and time savings. He would benefit from additional user-friendly features like voice-to-text for bids, and easy-to-understand reports that reduce the risk of costly errors.

James

: Needs enterprise-level integrations and dashboards. Beam AI can position itself as a strategic enabler for large teams and firms, focusing on scalability, data management, and integration into larger project management systems.

Market Segment Opportunity

General contractors like Ryan who are in the early stages of scaling. They need a mix of automation with human oversight, and a clear ROI to justify spending.

Estimators in mid-market commercial contracting firms who require high-volume accuracy and workflow efficiency. This segment demands seamless integrations with existing software.

Subcontractors who need tools to boost efficiency without investing in full-time staff. They’re often small businesses and will respond well to time-saving features.

Large commercial contractors who value speed, scalability, and data integrity. Beam AI should prioritize advanced reporting and integration tools to meet enterprise needs.

Potential Upsell Opportunities

Offering a tiered pricing model based on the size of the GC's business, with an add-on for real-time collaborative features.

Providing premium support or custom-built integrations for PlanSwift, Excel, and other estimating tools.

Introducing mobile app enhancements and additional AI-powered tools for specialized subcontractor needs (e.g., drywall-specific features).

Offering enterprise pricing models for large teams with features like multi-user access, audit trails, and advanced analytics.

Customer Retention Strategy

Ryan would benefit from a user-friendly onboarding process and regular check-ins with customer success to ensure he’s getting the most value.

Sarah would value regular product updates, particularly around integrations and reporting. Offering customer support focused on minimizing manual processes will drive retention.

Miguel is more likely to stay loyal if the tool is easy to use and addresses his specific trade needs. Simplified workflows and visual error reporting would help with retention.

James requires strong customer support and product customization. Offering personalized onboarding and a roadmap for scaling up with enterprise features would enhance retention.

Feedback Loop

Actively seeking feedback on scope detection accuracy and feature customization. Could be used for new product features targeted at GC firms.

Focus on gathering feedback regarding PlanSwift integrations and ease of use. Build features that fit seamlessly into her fast-paced workflow.

Regular feedback on the ease of use for estimating tools and the mobile app’s accuracy in the field.

Feedback on enterprise-level tools such as historical bid comparators, dashboards, and team management features for scaling large estimating teams.
